subject.title: Telegram delivery should be idempotent across message.send, final replies, and resumed turns

question: For Telegram sends whose server-side success is ambiguous, should OpenClaw prefer possible duplicate retry, possible message loss by quarantining the send, or suppression only when an authoritative server-owned receipt exists?
rationale: Deterministic duplicate paths already have targeted guards, but true at-most-once behavior under ambiguous network failure changes the reliability contract and cannot be selected safely from source evidence alone.

options.title: Receipt-Backed Suppression
options.body: Suppress later delivery only when a server-owned turn, outbox, transport, or transcript receipt proves that the visible result was delivered; quarantine ambiguous recovery separately.

options.title: Prefer Delivery Retry
options.body: Retain at-least-once recovery semantics and accept that an ambiguous Telegram failure may occasionally produce a duplicate.

options.title: Prefer No Duplicates
options.body: Never replay ambiguous Telegram sends and accept that some generated replies may be lost when delivery success cannot be confirmed.

recommendation.title: Receipt-Backed Suppression
recommendation.body: Suppress later delivery only when a server-owned turn, outbox, transport, or transcript receipt proves that the visible result was delivered; quarantine ambiguous recovery separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows direct ownership of the canonical final-payload and Telegram-visible delivery boundary.
